domain: team dinner at a Japanese izakaya
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a team dinner this Saturday at a Japanese izakaya. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Four of us initially: me, Sarah, Dev, and Marcus
Dev ate shrimp tempura at a work event last year and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
How many should I book the reservation for?
Marcus just messaged me — turns out he got retested and his doctor says he doesn't actually have celiac, it was a misdiagnosis. He can eat whatever he wants now
Marcus wants to bring his wife Priya too
Sarah just told me she's not feeling well and won't make it. She asked if I could bring her back some food though
Oh, Dev's brother Tom wants to join us too, so that's five now
Tom had a really bad reaction to peanuts when he was a kid, his mom always made sure there were none around
The izakaya has these dishes I'm eyeing: salmon sashimi, chicken karaage, shrimp gyoza, cold tofu with peanut sauce, and beef teriyaki with soy glaze. Any issues with these for our group?

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or raw seafood
inference_chain: Pregnancy → avoid raw fish/seafood due to listeria and mercury risk

constraints.surface_form: Dev ate shrimp tempura at a work event last year and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Tom had a really bad reaction to peanuts when he was a kid, his mom always made sure there were none around

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up in a strict Jain household in Gujarat and still follows all the practices
inference_chain: Strict Jain household → follows Jain dietary laws
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potato)

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a team dinner at a Japanese izakaya. You will introduce your group (Sarah, Dev, Marcus) with their constraints, then the group changes: Marcus's celiac is removed (misdiagnosis), Sarah leaves but wants takeaway, Marcus's wife Priya joins (Jain), and Dev's brother Tom joins late (peanut allergy). At the end you will list 5 specific dishes and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, cooperative team organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Sarah told me...', 'Dev mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination among friends.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

ground_truth.answer: Shrimp gyoza is problematic for Dev (shrimp allergy — anaphylactic). Cold tofu with peanut sauce is problematic for Tom (severe peanut allergy). Chicken karaage is problematic for Priya (Jain — no meat). Beef teriyaki is problematic for Priya (Jain — no meat). Salmon sashimi is fine for the table but must NOT be packed for Sarah's takeaway (she is pregnant — no raw fish). The soy glaze on beef teriyaki is NOT a problem — Marcus's celiac was a misdiagnosis, he can eat gluten now.
required_elements: Shrimp gyoza is problematic: Dev has a shrimp allergy (throat swelled up, EpiPen used)
Cold tofu with peanut sauce is problematic: Tom has a severe peanut allergy
Chicken karaage is problematic: Priya is Jain and cannot eat meat
Beef teriyaki is problematic: Priya is Jain and cannot eat meat
Salmon sashimi is fine for the table but must be excluded from Sarah's takeaway because she is pregnant and cannot eat raw fish
Marcus has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent does not flag gluten or soy as a problem for him
forbidden_elements: Flagging gluten or soy as a problem for Marcus (his celiac was a misdiagnosis, restriction removed)
Saying salmon sashimi is problematic for the table (Sarah is not at the table, she only gets takeaway)
Saying Dev has a general seafood allergy (he specifically reacted to shrimp only)
Ignoring Tom's peanut allergy on the cold tofu with peanut sauce (late-joiner must be tracked)
Ignoring Priya's Jain constraint on chicken karaage or beef teriyaki
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns at a Japanese izakaya. The agent must track: (1) Sarah is pregnant → no raw fish (inferential, never explicitly stated as a food rule), (2) Dev has a shrimp allergy (direct from EpiPen story — must NOT over-generalize to all seafood), (3) Marcus's celiac is REMOVED mid-conversation (misdiagnosis), (4) Priya joins late with an inferential constraint (strict Jain household → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables), (5) Tom joins LATE with a peanut allergy (primary failure mode — models forget late-joining entities), (6) Sarah EXITS the dinner but still needs takeaway (her pregnancy/raw fish constraint applies to takeaway only). At probe time, the current constraint state is: Dev=shrimp allergy, Tom=peanut allergy, Priya=Jain (no meat/fish/eggs/root veg), Sarah=pregnant (no raw fish, takeaway only). Marcus has NO restrictions. The over-generalization trap is Dev's shrimp allergy — salmon sashimi contains no shrimp and is fine for the table. The removed-constraint trap is Marcus's celiac — soy glaze is fine. The late-joiner trap is Tom — peanut sauce must be caught. The scope-distinction trap is salmon sashimi — fine for table, not for Sarah's takeaway.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
